findings.location: design.md#Decision: Birth dates live on the profile
findings.recommendation: Tie retention to the purpose (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), storage limitation): a member who opts out of birthday greetings still has `birthday` and `phone` kept on `profiles` for the whole life of the profile, with no use left for them. Add a requirement and a scenario "A member opts out → `birthday` and `phone` are erased", clear both columns on opt-out and on account deletion, and state how long the nightly backups that hold them are kept and when erased values leave them. Add the matching task in tasks.md.
findings.title: Birthday and phone kept after opt-out, backups with no expiry

findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Data minimisation (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)): delivering a birthday text needs only the phone number and the message; posting `display_name` with it hands an identifying detail to a US processor and lets it link the number to a named person. Send only the phone number and a generic message, or, if the name must appear, render the message text on our side and record why in the design.
findings.title: Display name sent to Textly beyond what the SMS needs

findings.evidence:
phone number and display name to Textly's API (hosted in the United
States), which sends the message.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Greetings are sent by SMS through Textly
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: Textly becomes a processor (GDPR Art. 28) receiving phone numbers in a third country (Chapter V). State in the design the processing agreement and the transfer mechanism (adequacy decision / Data Privacy Framework certification, or standard contractual clauses), and how long Textly keeps phone numbers and message logs. Only the controller can say what was decided.
findings.title: Transfer to Textly in the United States has no stated safeguard

findings.evidence: Members enjoy being remembered; marketing wants birthday messages.
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the purpose is marketing messages by SMS, which under ePrivacy rules for electronic marketing usually requires consent. State in the proposal that the opt-in is the consent (GDPR Art. 6(1)(a)), that it is freely withdrawable from the profile form, and that withdrawal stops the job and triggers the erasure of R-privacy-1.
findings.title: Lawful basis of the birthday processing not stated
